question.text: An electron in a hydrogen atom revolves around its nucleus with a speed of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>76</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>–</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> in an orbit of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>52</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Å</mi></math>. The magnetic field produced at the nucleus of the hydrogen atom is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>.

solution.text:
The magnetic field due to the electron is given by 

B=μ0qvsin90°4πr2

The given data is 

v=6.76×106 m s-1r=0.52×10-10 m

Thus, the magnetic field is 

B=10-7×1.6××10-19×6.76×1060.52×0.52×10-20=40 T
